analysis: Examined three changes. (1) NativeToolStreamRouter.swift line 188 (head): the forced-tool-choice branch now skips framing-whitespace-only visible text on every path, not only when native channels are used. isFramingWhitespace (ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift line 36) accepts only ASCII space, tab, LF and CR, so invisible Unicode characters are not smuggled through. Any other visible text still throws toolChoiceViolation before it is emitted. Whitespace-only output with no call is still rejected downstream, per the added test expecting 'model did not emit the required tool call'. The change drops only whitespace, so it exposes no prompt data and does not touch the encryption or coordinator boundaries (TB-002, A-001). (2) ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift lines 91-107 (head): advertisesCapability now admits four exact model IDs (Qwen3.5-9B, qwen3.5-35b-a3b, qwen3.6-35b-a3b-vl-mtp-mxfp8, mimo-v2.6-flash-mopd). Each is bound to an exact model_type, so a renamed or retyped artifact is not advertised. This widens the set of models the coordinator may route forced tool requests to. The forced path remains prompt-forced, withheld and schema-validated. forcedStrategy already routes qwen3_5 and mimo_v2 to structuredPostValidation, and validateParser requires the matching parser. Model-ID matching is case-sensitive and exact, which is conservative. This is a capability advertisement only, not a trust or attestation grant (T-052 is unaffected). The open assumption is that the coordinator derives routing from this advertisement and that model IDs map to verified weight hashes (T-027, T-012). That mapping is outside the supplied evidence. (3) EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift: tests only, with no production impact. Integration questions remain: how model-ID spoofing by a provider operator is bounded by the weight-hash verification already in the threat model, and whether the MiMo non-Qwen path with a Qwen-style tool newline matches the new whitespace skip. No concrete regression identified.
